notes: 1. SCOPE: This module covers (a) the Buyer-side 'Schedule a Call' / 'Reschedule Call' request modal on the Home Dashboard, and (b) the token-based post-call 'Call Feedback' form (FS Feature 2). The buyer only SUBMITS a request and later SUBMITS feedback; the assignment/scheduling/completion workflow runs on the SM Portal and is verified here only at its buyer-observable edges (notification received, status shown).

2. ENTRY POINT (live UI): Callback Request is NOT a separate page. It is a modal dialog opened from a button in the top-right of the Home Dashboard (https://uat.xrportal.in/home). The URL does NOT change when the modal opens. Source: visual-memory/buyer/callback-request/INDEX.md + callback-schedule-modal.png / callback-modal-verify-2026-06-06.png.

3. HEADER BUTTON STATE MACHINE (live UI): State 1 (no open request) = button text 'Schedule a Call' (white/default) -> opens the 'Schedule a Call' modal. State 2 (request already submitted) = button text 'Call Requested' (amber/orange badge) -> opens the 'Reschedule Call' modal. There is no third button; the same header control toggles between the two states.

4. SCHEDULE/RESCHEDULE MODAL FIELDS (live UI, exactly two): (a) 'Preferred Date & Time' - a single combined datetime picker, marked required with a red asterisk (*), pre-filled with the current date/time (captured as '04 Jun 2026, 17:00'), with a calendar icon on the right; (b) 'Comment (optional)' - a textarea, placeholder 'Any specific query or message for the callback...', maxlength 200 with a live '0 / 200' character counter. Buttons: 'Cancel' (closes) and 'Submit Request' (green) on the Schedule modal; 'Cancel' and 'Reschedule' (green) on the Reschedule modal. There is an X close icon top-right of the dialog.

5. DOC_DRIFT-001 - The FS/FRD list the Callback Request URLs as /call-feedback and /call-feedback/:code. Those routes are the POST-CALL FEEDBACK pages, NOT the callback REQUEST entry. The live request feature is a modal on /home with no route change (visual-memory INDEX.md 'Important Discovery': there is NO dedicated /call-feedback or callback page for the request; the standard sidebar shows no 'Callback' link). Live UI wins. TCs use the observed modal-on-/home entry; the /call-feedback/:code route is exercised only by the Call Feedback sub-module.

6. DOC_DRIFT-002 - FS 1.4 lists THREE separate fields (Request description / Preferred date / Preferred time) and marks all of them as NOT required. The live modal shows only TWO controls: a single combined 'Preferred Date & Time' picker that is marked REQUIRED (red asterisk) and pre-filled, plus an optional 'Comment'. So (i) date and time are one field, not two; (ii) 'description' is labelled 'Comment'; (iii) the date/time field is required on screen, contradicting 'all optional'. Live UI wins. Submit-with-blank-date behaviour is tested as a UI-blocked required-field case (TC_CALLBACK_VAL_003); FS-claimed 'all optional, blank submit succeeds' is retained as a [VERIFY WITH DEV] backend case (BYR_CB_015).

7. DOC_DRIFT-003 - FRD/FS mention a 'Schedule VC' / video-call option alongside the callback request. No such control appears in the live UI - only 'Schedule a Call'. The video-call path is treated as not-present-in-UI and is flagged [VERIFY WITH DEV]; no positive VC TC is asserted against the current build.

8. SILENT-UX-IS-NOT-A-BUG: A successful submit may navigate/close the modal and flip the header to 'Call Requested' WITHOUT necessarily showing a toast. Do NOT flag a missing success toast as a defect until the backend side-effect is verified - confirm the callback row was created (status REQUESTED, linked to the registration) and/or the header state changed. See feedback memory feedback_silent_ux_not_bug.md.

9. MUTATION AUTHORISATION: Submitting a callback request WRITES a DB row (callback_requests) and may notify a Sales Manager (WhatsApp via Botspice/Kaleyra). Reschedule mutates that row; feedback submission sets isBuyerFeedbackSubmitted=true. Every TC that submits / reschedules / submits feedback is marked [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] and requires explicit user authorisation before running on UAT (UAT accounts are stateful - CLAUDE.md Pipeline Discipline rule 7). Capture-only steps (open modal, view fields, read counter, Cancel/close) are safe.

10. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] = a disposable UAT record/state must be supplied before executing this destructive/stateful test (e.g. a registration with no open callback so the button reads 'Schedule a Call'; a registration already in 'Call Requested' state for reschedule; a valid unused buyerFeedbackToken URL; an SM-completed call to reach the feedback step; an API bearer token / another buyer's registration for ownership tests).
11. [VERIFY WITH DEV] = behaviour not confirmed in BRD/FRD/FS or not observable on the current UAT build; confirm before treating Pass/Fail as authoritative.

12. ASSIGNMENT RULE: The system assigns the request to a Sales Manager via the LEAST-LOADED algorithm (the SM with the fewest active requests). Round-robin code is DISABLED at callback-request-sm.service.js:338-349 (FSD-CORRECTION 2026-05-25). An SM must have isAvailable=true to receive an assignment.

13. STATUS LIFECYCLE: A new request starts at status REQUESTED (FS 1.5 Rule 4). The SM then schedules (buyer is notified) and completes the call. Both SM feedback (isSmFeedbackSubmitted) and buyer feedback (isBuyerFeedbackSubmitted) must be complete for the request to reach COMPLETED (FS 2.5 Rule 4). Baseline TCs flag a schema drift where COMPLETED is effectively unreachable and the row stays CONFIRMED (BYR_CB_030, BYR_CB_044) - retained as [VERIFY WITH DEV].

14. FEEDBACK FLOW: After the SM completes the call, a unique token URL /call-feedback/:code is sent to the buyer by SMS/WhatsApp. It is token-authenticated (no login), single-use per request, and expires - submitting sets isBuyerFeedbackSubmitted=true. Feedback form fields: Call rating (REQUIRED) + Comments (optional). FS 2.5.

15. AUTH: Buyer portal host is https://uat.xrportal.in/ (NOT uat-web). Mobile-OTP only; UAT mobile 8888888888 / static OTP 147258. Session is a JWT held in storage. The feedback link is the only callback surface reachable without login.

16. GLOSSARY: 'Schedule a Call' = header button (no open request) / Schedule modal submit context; 'Submit Request' = green submit on the Schedule modal; 'Call Requested' = amber header button (request open) that opens the Reschedule modal; 'Reschedule' = green submit on the Reschedule modal; 'Preferred Date & Time' = the single required datetime picker; 'Comment' = optional 200-char textarea; 'Call Feedback' = the post-call token page at /call-feedback/:code with a Call rating + Comments.

tcs.scenario: To verify the Schedule a Call button is visible
tcs.description: Verify that the 'Schedule a Call' button is shown in the Home Dashboard header for an authenticated buyer who has no open callback request.
tcs.precond: A buyer is logged in and on the Home Dashboard (/home) with NO open callback request. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a registration in the no-open-callback state.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in to the Buyer portal (8888888888 / 147258).
2. Land on the Home Dashboard.
3. Look at the top-right of the header.
tcs.expected: A 'Schedule a Call' button is shown in the top-right of the Home Dashboard header. The URL stays https://uat.xrportal.in/home (no route change). (Source: visual-memory callback-schedule-modal.png — header button top-right.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the Request Callback control is present on the portal
tcs.description: Verify that the callback request control is present and reachable on the Buyer portal (rendered as the 'Schedule a Call' header button on Home, per live UI).
tcs.precond: A buyer is logged in and on the Home Dashboard.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in to the Buyer portal.
2. On Home, look for the callback request control.
tcs.expected: The callback request control is present — in the live build it is the 'Schedule a Call' button in the Home header (FS calls it 'Request Callback'). It may also appear as a floating button or nav item per FS, but the confirmed live location is the Home header (DOC_DRIFT-001). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm no additional floating/nav entry point exists.

tcs.scenario: To verify the Call Requested amber state after submission
tcs.description: Verify that once a request exists, the header button reads 'Call Requested' in amber/orange instead of 'Schedule a Call'.
tcs.precond: The logged-in buyer's registration already has an open callback request. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a registration in the 'Call Requested' state.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in as a buyer whose registration has an open callback request.
2. Land on the Home Dashboard.
3. Look at the header button.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] registration with an open callback request
tcs.expected: The header button reads 'Call Requested' and is shown in an amber/orange badge style (not the default white 'Schedule a Call'). (Source: visual-memory callback-modal-verify-2026-06-06.png — header shows 'Call Requested'.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the header button routes by state (state machine)
tcs.description: Verify that the single header control opens the Schedule modal when no request exists and the Reschedule modal when a request is open.
tcs.precond: Access to one registration with no open request and one with an open request. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] both registration states.
tcs.steps:
1. As a buyer with NO open request, click the header button and read the modal title.
2. Close it.
3. As a buyer WITH an open request, click the header button and read the modal title.
tcs.expected: In the no-open-request state the button is 'Schedule a Call' and opens the 'Schedule a Call' modal; in the open-request state the button is 'Call Requested' and opens the 'Reschedule Call' modal. The same header control routes by request state.

tcs.scenario: To verify the Submit button is visible

tcs.steps: 1. Look at the bottom of the modal.
tcs.expected: A green 'Submit Request' button is visible at the bottom-right of the modal, next to a grey 'Cancel' button.

tcs.scenario: To verify the Comment field supports multiline input
tcs.description: Verify that the Comment field is a multi-line textarea that accepts line breaks.

tcs.steps:

2. Type a line, press Enter, type a second line.
tcs.expected: The Comment field accepts multi-line text — pressing Enter creates a new line within the textarea (it is not single-line).

tcs.scenario: To verify the picker is pre-filled on open
tcs.description: Verify that the Preferred Date & Time field is pre-filled with the current date/time when the modal opens.
tcs.precond: The Schedule a Call modal is freshly opened.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the Schedule a Call modal.
2. Read the value in the Preferred Date & Time field.
tcs.expected: The Preferred Date & Time field is already populated with a date/time value on open (captured as '04 Jun 2026, 17:00'); the field is not blank. (Source: callback-schedule-modal.png.)

tcs.scenario: To verify clicking the field opens a calendar/time picker
tcs.description: Verify that clicking the field (or its calendar icon) opens a calendar/time selection control.
tcs.precond: The Schedule a Call modal is open.
tcs.steps: 1. Click the Preferred Date & Time field (or the calendar icon on the right).
tcs.expected: A calendar/time picker control opens, allowing the buyer to choose a date and a time.

tcs.scenario: To verify today and future dates are selectable
tcs.description: Verify that the current date and future dates can be selected in the picker.
tcs.precond: The date/time picker is open.
tcs.steps:
1. Select today's date.
2. Select a date a few days in the future.
tcs.expected: Today and future dates are selectable and update the Preferred Date & Time field accordingly.

tcs.scenario: To verify the time can be set (hour and minute)
tcs.description: Verify that the picker lets the buyer set an hour and minute for the preferred call time.
tcs.precond: The date/time picker is open.
tcs.steps:
1. Set a specific hour.
2. Set a specific minute.
3. Confirm the selection.
tcs.expected: The chosen hour and minute are applied to the Preferred Date & Time field (e.g. shows '... 11:30').

tcs.scenario: To verify past dates are greyed out / unselectable
tcs.description: Verify that dates earlier than today cannot be chosen in the picker.
tcs.precond: The date/time picker is open.
tcs.steps: 1. Try to select a date before today.
tcs.expected: Past dates are greyed out / unselectable so a callback cannot be requested for a date already gone. [VERIFY WITH DEV] FS does not state a past-date restriction in the UI; confirm whether the picker disables past dates or relies on the backend (BYR_CB_035).

tcs.scenario: To verify a past requestedAt is rejected by the backend
tcs.description: Verify that a request whose preferred date/time is in the past is rejected by the backend.
tcs.precond: Ability to submit a request with a past requestedAt (UI bypass or API). [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access; user authorisation to submit.
tcs.steps:
1. Submit a callback request with a Preferred Date & Time set in the past.
2. Read the response.
tcs.expected: The backend rejects a past requestedAt with a validation error and creates no callback row. [VERIFY WITH DEV] FS does not document a past-date rule; confirm the backend enforces it.

tcs.scenario: To verify weekend dates are handled per configuration
tcs.description: Verify how the picker treats weekend/Sunday dates if a business-day restriction is configured.
tcs.precond: The date/time picker is open.
tcs.steps: 1. Try to select a Sunday / weekend date.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] FS does not document any weekend/business-day restriction. [To verify] confirm whether weekends are disabled or freely selectable; the current expectation is that all future dates are selectable unless a config disables weekends.

tcs.scenario: To verify the time picker honours a business-hours window
tcs.description: Verify whether the time picker limits selectable hours to a business window if configured.
tcs.precond: The date/time picker is open.
tcs.steps: 1. Try to select an out-of-hours time (e.g. 03:00).
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] FS does not document a business-hours window. [To verify] confirm whether hours are limited to a business window or any time is selectable; current expectation is any time is selectable.

tcs.scenario: To verify Comment is optional
tcs.description: Verify that leaving the Comment textarea empty does not block submission (Comment is optional).
tcs.precond: The Schedule a Call modal is open with a valid Preferred Date & Time. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] user authorisation to submit a request.
tcs.steps:
1. Leave the Comment field empty.
2. Click Submit Request.
tcs.expected: Submission is allowed with an empty Comment; no 'comment required' error is shown. (Comment is labelled 'optional'.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the Comment field is optional (label)
tcs.description: Verify that the Comment field is explicitly marked optional in the modal.
tcs.precond: The Schedule a Call modal is open.
tcs.steps: 1. Read the Comment field label.
tcs.expected: The label reads 'Comment (optional)', confirming the field is not required.

tcs.scenario: To verify Comment accepts up to 200 chars with a live counter
tcs.description: Verify that the Comment textarea accepts up to 200 characters and the character counter updates live as the buyer types.
tcs.precond: The Schedule a Call modal is open.
tcs.steps:
1. Type text into the Comment field and watch the counter.
2. Continue typing toward 200 characters.
tcs.expected: The counter updates live (e.g. '12 / 200', as seen in callback-modal-verify-2026-06-06.png) and the field accepts text up to 200 characters.

tcs.scenario: To verify the Comment 200-character limit is enforced
tcs.description: Verify that the Comment field does not accept more than 200 characters.
tcs.precond: The Schedule a Call modal is open.
tcs.steps:
1. Type or paste more than 200 characters into the Comment field.
2. Read the field value and the counter.
tcs.expected: The field caps at 200 characters (counter stops at '200 / 200'); extra characters are blocked or trimmed (maxlength 200).

tcs.scenario: To verify the counter resets to 0 / 200 on reopen
tcs.description: Verify that the character counter reads '0 / 200' on a fresh modal open and again after a Cancel/reopen cycle.
tcs.precond: The Schedule a Call modal can be opened and closed.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the modal and read the counter.
2. Type some text, then click Cancel.
3. Reopen the modal and read the counter again.
tcs.expected: On first open the counter reads '0 / 200'; after Cancel and reopen the Comment field is empty and the counter again reads '0 / 200'.

tcs.scenario: To verify HTML/script in the Comment is sanitised
tcs.description: Verify that HTML or script tags entered in the Comment are sanitised/escaped and not executed.
tcs.precond: The Schedule a Call modal is open. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] user authorisation to submit.
tcs.steps:
1. Type '<script>alert(1)</script>' into the Comment field.
2. Submit the request (if authorised) and view the stored/displayed comment.
tcs.expected: No script executes; the tags are escaped/sanitised on submit and stored/displayed as inert text. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm server-side sanitisation of the comment field.

tcs.scenario: To verify Submit succeeds with date only (no comment)
tcs.description: Verify that submitting the Schedule modal with only the Preferred Date & Time set (no comment) creates the request.
tcs.precond: The Schedule a Call modal is open with a valid date/time and no comment. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a registration with no open request; user authorisation to submit.
tcs.steps:
1. Keep the pre-filled Preferred Date & Time (or pick one).
2. Leave Comment empty.
3. Click Submit Request.
tcs.expected: The request is created; the modal closes and the header button flips to 'Call Requested' (amber). A success toast may or may not appear — silent-UX-is-not-a-bug (note 8): verify the callback row was created at status REQUESTED before flagging a missing toast.

tcs.scenario: To verify Submit succeeds with datetime + comment
tcs.description: Verify that submitting with both a Preferred Date & Time and a comment creates the request and persists the comment.
tcs.precond: The Schedule a Call modal is open. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a registration with no open request; user authorisation to submit.
tcs.steps:
1. Set a Preferred Date & Time.
2. Type a comment (e.g. 'Please call about home loan').
3. Click Submit Request.
tcs.testData: Valid date/time; Comment: 'Please call about home loan'; [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED]
tcs.expected: The request is created with the chosen date/time and comment stored; the modal closes and the header shows 'Call Requested'. (Verify the side-effect per note 8.)

tcs.scenario: To verify submit with all fields filled succeeds
tcs.description: Verify the happy-path submission with every field populated.
tcs.precond: The Schedule a Call modal is open. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] no-open-request registration; user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Set the Preferred Date & Time.
2. Enter a comment.
3. Click Submit Request.
4. Observe the result.
tcs.expected: The callback request is submitted successfully and linked to the buyer's current registration (status REQUESTED); the header reflects 'Call Requested'.

tcs.scenario: To verify backend behaviour when all fields are blank
tcs.description: Verify the FS-claimed 'all fields optional' behaviour at the backend versus the live UI required date/time.
tcs.precond: Ability to submit with no date/time (UI bypass or API). [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access; user authorisation.
tcs.steps: 1. Attempt to submit a callback request with no Preferred Date & Time and no comment.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] FS 1.4 says all fields are optional, but the live UI marks Preferred Date & Time required (DOC_DRIFT-002) and the backend rejects a missing requestedAt (BYR_CB_051). Confirm which is authoritative: the live UI blocks the all-blank submit; the backend is expected to reject a missing requestedAt rather than create an empty request.

tcs.scenario: To verify Submit is blocked when date/time is cleared
tcs.description: Verify that clearing the required Preferred Date & Time blocks submission with a validation message.
tcs.precond: The Schedule a Call modal is open.
tcs.steps:
1. Clear the Preferred Date & Time field.
2. Click Submit Request.
tcs.expected: Submission is blocked — a required-field validation is shown for Preferred Date & Time (red asterisk field) and no request is created. (DOC_DRIFT-002: the field is required in the live UI.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the backend rejects a missing requestedAt
tcs.description: Verify that a submit with no requestedAt is rejected by the backend (UI bypass / API).
tcs.precond: API access or a way to submit without a date. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Send a create-callback request with requestedAt omitted/null.
2. Read the response.
tcs.expected: The backend returns a validation error (e.g. 400) and creates no row. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the exact error and that requestedAt is server-side required.

tcs.scenario: To verify the backend rejects a missing registrationNumber
tcs.description: Verify that a create-callback without a registration reference is rejected.
tcs.precond: API access. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Send a create-callback request with registrationNumber omitted.
2. Read the response.
tcs.expected: The backend rejects the request (the callback must be linked to a registration per FS 1.5 Rule 1) and creates no row. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the error code/message.

tcs.scenario: To verify a double-click does not submit twice
tcs.description: Verify that double-clicking Submit Request does not create two callback rows.
tcs.precond: The Schedule a Call modal is open with valid input. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] no-open-request registration; user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Fill the form.
2. Double-click Submit Request quickly.
3. Check how many requests were created.
tcs.expected: Only one callback request is created; the button disables / guards against a duplicate submission on the second click. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the button is disabled during the in-flight call.

tcs.scenario: To verify a network failure on submit shows a retry option
tcs.description: Verify that if the submit API fails (network/500), the buyer sees an error with a way to retry and no orphaned state.
tcs.precond: The Schedule a Call modal is open; the submit endpoint can be made to fail. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] fault injection; user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Fill the form.
2. Force the submit request to fail (offline / blocked endpoint).
3. Click Submit Request.
4. Observe the modal.
tcs.expected: An error message is shown, the modal stays open with the entered values, and the buyer can retry the submit; no callback row is created on the failed attempt. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the exact error string and retry affordance.

tcs.scenario: To verify the post-submit confirmation feedback
tcs.description: Verify the confirmation feedback shown to the buyer after a successful submission.
tcs.precond: A request has just been submitted. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] user authorisation to submit.
tcs.steps:
1. Submit a valid callback request.
2. Observe any toast/confirmation and the header state.
tcs.expected: The buyer receives confirmation that the request was submitted — at minimum the header flips to 'Call Requested'. A success toast may also appear. Per note 8 (silent-UX-is-not-a-bug), a missing toast is NOT a defect if the request row was created and the header state changed. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the intended success message.

tcs.scenario: To verify a duplicate active callback is rejected

2. Read the response.
tcs.expected: The second active callback for the same registration is rejected (the header shows 'Call Requested', so the UI routes to Reschedule rather than a new request). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the backend blocks a duplicate active callback per registration.

tcs.expected: The modal closes with no request created; the form state is discarded.

tcs.scenario: To verify the ESC key closes the modal
tcs.description: Verify that pressing ESC closes the modal without submitting.
tcs.precond: The Schedule a Call modal is open.
tcs.steps: 1. Press the ESC key.
tcs.expected: The modal closes without submitting. [VERIFY WITH DEV] ESC-to-close is not documented in FS; confirm it is wired and does not submit.

tcs.scenario: To verify a backdrop click does not accidentally submit
tcs.description: Verify that clicking the dimmed backdrop outside the modal does not submit the request.
tcs.precond: The Schedule a Call modal is open.
tcs.steps: 1. Click on the dimmed area outside the modal.
tcs.expected: The click does not submit the request. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm whether a backdrop click closes the modal or is ignored; in neither case must it submit.

tcs.scenario: To verify closing after partial entry shows no confirmation dialog
tcs.description: Verify that closing the modal after typing some data does not prompt a 'discard changes?' dialog (or, if it does, document it).
tcs.precond: The Schedule a Call modal is open with partial input.
tcs.steps:
1. Type a partial comment.
2. Click X / Cancel.
tcs.expected: The modal closes directly with no unsaved-changes confirmation prompt; entered data is discarded. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm there is no discard-confirmation dialog by design.

tcs.scenario: To verify reopening starts with an empty form
tcs.description: Verify that after closing and reopening, the Schedule modal starts fresh (no stale comment) with the date/time re-defaulted.
tcs.precond: The modal has been opened, typed into, and closed.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the modal, type a comment, close it.
2. Reopen the modal.
3. Inspect the fields.
tcs.expected: On reopen the Comment field is empty (counter '0 / 200') and the Preferred Date & Time is re-defaulted to the current date/time; no stale data carries over.

tcs.scenario: To verify modal data persists across a brief tab switch
tcs.description: Verify that switching browser tabs briefly and returning does not clear the in-progress modal data.
tcs.precond: The Schedule a Call modal is open with entered data.
tcs.steps:
1. Type a comment and set a date/time.
2. Switch to another browser tab for a few seconds.
3. Switch back.
tcs.expected: On returning, the modal is still open and the entered comment and date/time are preserved (no reset). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the modal is not remounted on visibility change.

tcs.scenario: To verify close during an in-flight submit is handled
tcs.description: Verify behaviour when the buyer clicks X while the submit API is still in flight.
tcs.precond: A submit has been triggered and the response is delayed. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] slow-network simulation; user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Click Submit Request.
2. While the request is in flight, click X.
3. Observe the result and the header state.
tcs.expected: Closing does not corrupt state — either the X is disabled until the API returns, or the in-flight submit still completes and the header reflects the true result (no duplicate, no orphaned partial). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the intended in-flight close behaviour.

tcs.scenario: To verify Call Requested opens the Reschedule modal
tcs.description: Verify that clicking the amber 'Call Requested' header button opens the Reschedule Call modal.
tcs.precond: The buyer's registration has an open callback request (header shows 'Call Requested'). [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a registration in the open-request state.
tcs.steps:
1. On Home, click the amber 'Call Requested' button.
2. Read the dialog title.
tcs.expected: A modal titled 'Reschedule Call' opens, with the same field layout as the Schedule modal but a green 'Reschedule' button instead of 'Submit Request'. (Source: callback-modal-verify-2026-06-06.png.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the Reschedule modal field schema matches Schedule
tcs.description: Verify that the Reschedule Call modal has the same fields as the Schedule modal (Preferred Date & Time required + optional Comment) and the correct submit label.
tcs.precond: The Reschedule Call modal is open.
tcs.steps: 1. Look at the modal fields and buttons.
tcs.expected: The Reschedule modal shows the same 'Preferred Date & Time' (required) picker and 'Comment (optional)' textarea with a '... / 200' counter, plus a grey 'Cancel' and a green 'Reschedule' button. (Source: callback-modal-verify-2026-06-06.png — counter shows '12 / 200'.)

tcs.scenario: To verify Reschedule with a new datetime updates the call
tcs.description: Verify that submitting the Reschedule modal with a new Preferred Date & Time updates the existing request.
tcs.precond: The Reschedule Call modal is open on an existing request. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] open-request registration; user authorisation to reschedule.
tcs.steps:
1. Change the Preferred Date & Time to a new value.
2. Optionally update the comment.
3. Click Reschedule.
tcs.expected: The existing callback request is updated with the new date/time (and comment if changed); the modal closes and the header still reads 'Call Requested'. (Verify the row was updated per note 8.)

tcs.scenario: To verify Cancel in Reschedule leaves the request unchanged
tcs.description: Verify that clicking Cancel in the Reschedule modal closes it without altering the existing request.
tcs.precond: The Reschedule Call modal is open.
tcs.steps:
1. Change a field.
2. Click Cancel.
3. Reopen the Reschedule modal.
tcs.expected: The modal closes with no change persisted; the existing request keeps its original date/time and the header still reads 'Call Requested'.

tcs.scenario: To verify Reschedule is blocked when date/time is cleared
tcs.description: Verify that clearing the required Preferred Date & Time in the Reschedule modal blocks the Reschedule action.
tcs.precond: The Reschedule Call modal is open.
tcs.steps:
1. Clear the Preferred Date & Time field.
2. Click Reschedule.
tcs.expected: Reschedule is blocked — a required-field validation is shown for Preferred Date & Time and the existing request is not modified.

tcs.scenario: To verify reschedule is only allowed at status REQUESTED
tcs.description: Verify that the buyer can reschedule only while the request is still at status REQUESTED (not after the SM has scheduled/completed).
tcs.precond: Requests at different statuses are available. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] requests at REQUESTED and at a later status.
tcs.steps:
1. With a REQUESTED request, open Reschedule and confirm it is editable.
2. With a scheduled/completed request, check whether reschedule is offered.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] requests at REQUESTED and at a later status
tcs.expected: Reschedule is available while the request is REQUESTED; once the SM has scheduled/completed, the buyer can no longer reschedule. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the exact statuses at which reschedule is allowed/blocked.

tcs.scenario: To verify there is no buyer-side cancellation endpoint
tcs.description: Verify the documented limitation that the buyer cannot cancel a callback request (only reschedule).
tcs.precond: A buyer has an open callback request. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access to probe for a cancel endpoint.
tcs.steps:
1. Inspect the UI for a cancel/withdraw control on the open request.
2. Probe the API for a buyer cancel endpoint.
tcs.expected: There is no buyer-facing cancel/withdraw action — the only buyer action on an open request is Reschedule. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm no buyer-side cancellation endpoint exists.

tcs.scenario: To verify a new request starts at status REQUESTED
tcs.description: Verify that a freshly created callback request has status REQUESTED.
tcs.precond: A request was just created. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] DB/admin read access to the request status; user authorisation to submit.
tcs.steps:
1. Submit a callback request.
2. Inspect its status (DB / SM view / API).
tcs.expected: The new request's status is REQUESTED (FS 1.5 Rule 4).

tcs.scenario: To verify assignment uses the least-loaded algorithm
tcs.description: Verify that the request is assigned to an available SM with the fewest active requests (least-loaded), NOT round-robin.
tcs.precond: Multiple available SMs with differing active-request counts. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] SM fixtures with known loads; admin/DB read access.
tcs.steps:
1. Note each available SM's active-request count.
2. Submit a new callback request.
3. Inspect which SM it was assigned to.
tcs.expected: The request is assigned to the available SM with the fewest active requests (least-loaded). Round-robin is disabled at callback-request-sm.service.js:338-349 (FSD-CORRECTION). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm assignment against the live build.

tcs.scenario: To verify the request is linked to the current registration
tcs.description: Verify that a created callback request is linked to the buyer's current registration.
tcs.precond: A request was just created. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] DB read access; user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Submit a callback request from a specific registration.
2. Inspect the stored callback row's registration reference.
tcs.expected: The callback row references the buyer's current registration (FS 1.5 Rule 1).

tcs.scenario: To verify behaviour when no SM is available
tcs.description: Verify the documented edge where no SM is available — a row may be created with manager_id = NULL (flagged as a bug in baseline).
tcs.precond: No SM has isAvailable=true. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] all SMs unavailable; DB read access; user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. With no available SM, submit a callback request.
2. Inspect the created row's manager_id.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] Baseline flags that a row is created silently with manager_id = NULL when no SM is available (potential BUG). Confirm whether the request should be queued, rejected, or assigned later, versus the current silent NULL assignment.

tcs.scenario: To verify the request cannot reach COMPLETED (schema drift)
tcs.description: Verify the documented drift where a request stays at CONFIRMED and COMPLETED is effectively unreachable.
tcs.precond: A request that has gone through the full SM flow. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a fully-processed request; DB read access.
tcs.steps:
1. Drive a request through SM scheduling, call completion, and both feedbacks.
2. Inspect the final status.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] Baseline flags that the request stays at CONFIRMED rather than reaching COMPLETED (schema drift). Confirm the intended terminal status and whether COMPLETED is reachable per FS 2.5 Rule 4.

tcs.scenario: To verify the buyer is notified when the SM schedules
tcs.description: Verify that the buyer receives a notification once the SM schedules the meeting.
tcs.precond: An SM schedules the buyer's open request. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] an SM able to schedule; notification-log visibility.
tcs.steps:
1. Submit a callback request.
2. Have the SM schedule the meeting.
3. Check for a buyer notification.
tcs.expected: The buyer receives a notification when the SM schedules the meeting (FS 1.5 Rule 5). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the channel (in-app / WhatsApp / SMS) and the exact trigger.

tcs.scenario: To verify the create-callback WhatsApp template
tcs.description: Verify that creating a callback dispatches the expected WhatsApp template to the SM/customer (Botspice expert_customer_inform per baseline).
tcs.precond: A callback is created. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] outbound message-log access; user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Submit a callback request.
2. Inspect the outbound WhatsApp dispatch.
tcs.expected: A WhatsApp message is dispatched using the Botspice 'expert_customer_inform' template on create. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the template name and recipient against the live build (BRD lists Kaleyra for WhatsApp; baseline notes Botspice — reconcile).

tcs.scenario: To verify no notification fires on Cancel/close
tcs.description: Verify that simply opening and cancelling the modal (no submit) dispatches no SMS/WhatsApp/email.
tcs.precond: The Schedule a Call modal can be opened and cancelled. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] outbound message-log access.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the Schedule a Call modal.
2. Click Cancel / X without submitting.
3. Check outbound message logs.
tcs.expected: No SMS, WhatsApp or email is dispatched for an opened-and-cancelled modal — notifications fire only on an actual submit. (Silent-by-design for the non-submit path; note 8.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the feedback-link notification is dispatched after call completion
tcs.description: Verify that the token-based feedback link is sent to the buyer by SMS/WhatsApp after the SM completes the call.
tcs.precond: The SM has completed the call and submitted SM feedback. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] an SM-completed call; outbound message-log access.
tcs.steps:
1. Have the SM complete the call and submit feedback.
2. Check the buyer's outbound SMS/WhatsApp for the feedback link.
tcs.expected: A message containing the unique /call-feedback/:code link is sent to the buyer's mobile after call completion (FS 2.2 / 2.3). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the channel and template.

tcs.scenario: To verify the feedback URL is accessible without login
tcs.description: Verify that the token-based feedback page at /call-feedback/:code loads without requiring login.
tcs.precond: A valid, unused buyerFeedbackToken URL exists. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a valid feedback link.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the /call-feedback/:code link in a browser with no buyer session.
2. Observe the page.
tcs.expected: The feedback form loads without a login prompt (token-authenticated, no login required — FS 2.5 Rule 1).

tcs.scenario: To verify the feedback form fields
tcs.description: Verify that the Call Feedback form shows a required Call rating and an optional Comments field.
tcs.precond: A valid feedback link is open. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a valid feedback link.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the feedback link.
2. Note the fields and the submit control.
tcs.expected: The form shows a 'Call rating' control (required) and a 'Comments' field (optional), plus a Submit button (FS 2.4). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm exact on-screen labels and the rating control type.

tcs.scenario: To verify the Call rating field is mandatory
tcs.description: Verify that the feedback form cannot be submitted without a Call rating.
tcs.precond: The feedback form is open. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a valid feedback link.
tcs.steps:
1. Leave the rating unset.
2. Click Submit.
tcs.expected: Submission is blocked and a required-field validation is shown for Call rating (FS 2.4 — rating is required).

tcs.scenario: To verify the Comments field is optional
tcs.description: Verify that feedback can be submitted with only a rating and no comments.
tcs.precond: The feedback form is open. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a valid feedback link; user authorisation to submit.
tcs.steps:
1. Set a rating.
2. Leave Comments empty.
3. Click Submit.
tcs.expected: Submission succeeds with an empty Comments field (Comments is optional).

tcs.scenario: To verify submission sets isBuyerFeedbackSubmitted = true
tcs.description: Verify that submitting feedback sets the isBuyerFeedbackSubmitted flag.
tcs.precond: A valid feedback link and DB/admin read access. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] valid feedback link; DB read access; user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Submit the feedback form.
2. Inspect the callback record.
tcs.expected: The record's isBuyerFeedbackSubmitted is set to true after submission (FS 2.5 Rule 3).

tcs.scenario: To verify an invalid feedback token shows an error
tcs.description: Verify that opening the feedback page with an invalid/garbage token shows an error, not a usable form.
tcs.precond: An invalid token URL. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] an invalid token value.
tcs.steps:
1. Open /call-feedback/<invalid-token>.
2. Observe the page.
tcs.expected: An error state is shown (e.g. invalid/expired link) and no submittable feedback form is presented. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the exact error message.

tcs.scenario: To verify the feedback token cannot be reused
tcs.description: Verify that a feedback token is single-use — once feedback is submitted, the same link cannot be used again.
tcs.precond: A feedback link that has already been submitted once. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] an already-used feedback link.
tcs.steps:
1. Submit feedback via the link once.
2. Reopen the same link and attempt to submit again.
tcs.expected: The second use is rejected — the link shows an already-submitted/expired state and cannot submit again (FS 2.5 Rule 2 — token unique per request, cannot be reused).

tcs.scenario: To verify an in-app duplicate feedback submission is blocked
tcs.description: Verify that a duplicate feedback submission from the in-app path is blocked.
tcs.precond: A request whose feedback was already submitted. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a request with feedback already submitted.
tcs.steps:
1. With feedback already submitted, attempt to submit feedback again in-app.
2. Observe the result.
tcs.expected: The duplicate in-app submission is blocked (isBuyerFeedbackSubmitted already true). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the in-app block matches the token-page block (see BYR_CB_040).

tcs.scenario: To verify buyer feedback eligibility requires CONFIRMED + SM feedback
tcs.description: Verify that the buyer can submit feedback only once the request is CONFIRMED and the SM has submitted their feedback.
tcs.precond: Requests at varying states. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] requests with/without SM feedback.
tcs.steps:
1. Try to submit buyer feedback before SM feedback exists.
2. Try again after the SM has submitted feedback on a CONFIRMED request.
tcs.expected: Buyer feedback is only eligible when the request is CONFIRMED and isSmFeedbackSubmitted=1 (FS 2.3 precondition). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the exact eligibility gate.

tcs.scenario: To verify public-token vs in-app feedback eligibility differ (BUG)
tcs.description: Verify the baseline-flagged discrepancy where the public token link and the in-app feedback path apply different eligibility checks.
tcs.precond: A request reachable by both the token link and in-app. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] matching request states for both paths.
tcs.steps:
1. Check feedback eligibility via the public /call-feedback/:code link.
2. Check feedback eligibility for the same request via the in-app path.
3. Compare.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] Baseline flags that the public token link and the in-app path allow feedback under different conditions (potential BUG). Confirm whether the eligibility rules should be identical across both surfaces.

tcs.scenario: To verify a registration not owned by the buyer returns 404
tcs.description: Verify that creating a callback against a registration the buyer does not own is rejected (ownership check).
tcs.precond: An API bearer token for one buyer and a registration number belonging to a different buyer. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API token + another buyer's registration.
tcs.steps:
1. Call the create-callback API with another buyer's registrationNumber.
2. Read the response.
tcs.expected: The API returns 404 (registration not owned by the caller) and creates no callback row.

tcs.scenario: To verify a buyer query for status=COMPLETED returns 0 rows
tcs.description: Verify the baseline observation that querying the buyer's callbacks by status=COMPLETED returns no rows (COMPLETED unreachable — see BYR_CB_030).
tcs.precond: API access for a buyer with at least one fully-processed callback. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API token.
tcs.steps:
1. Call the buyer's callbacks API filtered by status=COMPLETED.
2. Read the response.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] The query returns 0 rows because requests stay at CONFIRMED rather than reaching COMPLETED (schema drift, BYR_CB_030). Confirm whether this is expected or a defect.

tcs.scenario: To verify the description column vs validator length mismatch
tcs.description: Verify the baseline-flagged mismatch where the DB description column allows 750 chars but the validator caps at 500.
tcs.precond: API access; ability to submit a long description. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API token.
tcs.steps:
1. Submit a callback with a description of ~600 characters.
2. Read the response and the stored value length.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] Baseline flags a mismatch: the DB description column is 750 but the validator caps at 500. Confirm the effective cap and whether the UI's 200-char comment limit is the true ceiling (DOC_DRIFT-002 — the live UI comment field is 200).

tcs.scenario: To verify the improvement-comments validator off-by-message bug
tcs.description: Verify the baseline-flagged bug where the improvement-comments validator caps at 900 but the error message states 1000.
tcs.precond: Access to the SM-side improvement-comments validation (downstream of the buyer flow). [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API/UI access to that field.
tcs.steps:
1. Submit an improvement comment of 901+ characters.
2. Read the validation error.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] Baseline flags that the validator caps at 900 while the error message says 1000 (message/limit mismatch BUG). Confirm the true cap and correct the message. (Note: this is an SM-side field reached from the callback flow; in scope only as a downstream edge.)

tcs.scenario: To verify followup datetime is required when followup is requested
tcs.description: Verify the rule that a followup datetime becomes required when followupCallRequired=true.
tcs.precond: Access to the followup path (SM-side, downstream of the callback). [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API/UI access.
tcs.steps:
1. Set followupCallRequired=true without a followup datetime.
2. Attempt to save.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] When followupCallRequired=true, a followup datetime is required and a missing value is rejected. Confirm the rule and error string. (SM-side downstream edge of the callback flow.)

tcs.scenario: To verify an unauthenticated user cannot open the modal
tcs.description: Verify that an unauthenticated user cannot reach the Home Dashboard and therefore cannot open the callback modal.
tcs.precond: No buyer session (storage cleared).
tcs.steps:
1. With no session, navigate directly to https://uat.xrportal.in/home.
2. Observe the result.
tcs.expected: The buyer is redirected to the login page (root /); the Home Dashboard and the 'Schedule a Call' control are not exposed without authentication.

tcs.scenario: To verify a tampered/expired JWT blocks the callback action
tcs.description: Verify that a tampered or expired buyer JWT causes the protected create-callback call to fail and the buyer to be sent to login.
tcs.precond: A logged-in buyer session. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] ability to tamper/expire the stored JWT.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the Schedule a Call modal.
2. Tamper with / expire the stored JWT.
3. Submit the request.
tcs.expected: The protected submit fails with 401 and the buyer is redirected to login; no callback row is created. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the redirect/refresh behaviour on 401.

tcs.scenario: To verify the create-callback API requires a valid token
tcs.description: Verify that the create-callback endpoint rejects an unauthenticated request.
tcs.precond: API client available. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Call the create-callback endpoint with no Authorization header.
2. Read the status.
tcs.expected: The endpoint returns 401 Unauthorized and creates no row.

tcs.scenario: To verify another buyer cannot reschedule someone else's request
tcs.description: Verify ownership isolation on reschedule — buyer A cannot modify buyer B's callback request.
tcs.precond: Two buyers' tokens and one request owned by buyer B. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] tokens for two buyers; a request owned by B.
tcs.steps:
1. As buyer A, call the reschedule/update endpoint for buyer B's callback request id.
2. Read the response.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] buyer A token + buyer B request id
tcs.expected: The request is rejected (403/404) — a buyer cannot reschedule or read another buyer's callback request (multi-tenant isolation). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the exact status.

tcs.scenario: To verify the modal renders on a mobile viewport
tcs.description: Verify that the Schedule a Call modal renders without overflow and stays usable on a phone viewport (the Buyer portal is mobile-first).
tcs.precond: A buyer is logged in; the browser is set to a 375x667 mobile viewport.
tcs.steps:
1. Set the viewport to 375x667.
2. Open the Schedule a Call modal.
3. Check the fields and buttons.
tcs.expected: The modal renders within the viewport with no horizontal overflow; the date/time picker, comment field, counter, Cancel and Submit Request remain reachable and tappable (mobile-first design — FRD 12).

tcs.scenario: To verify the modal is keyboard accessible
tcs.description: Verify that the modal can be operated by keyboard — focus is trapped in the dialog and Tab reaches every control.
tcs.precond: The Schedule a Call modal is open.
tcs.steps:
1. Press Tab repeatedly.
2. Observe focus order across the date/time field, comment, Cancel and Submit Request.
tcs.expected: Focus moves through all interactive controls and stays trapped within the dialog while open; ESC behaviour follows BYR_CB_023. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm focus-trap and visible focus indicators (not documented in FS).

tcs.scenario: To verify the full request -> reschedule buyer journey
tcs.description: Verify the complete buyer journey: open Schedule modal, submit a request, see 'Call Requested', reopen as Reschedule, change the time, and confirm the update.
tcs.precond: A buyer with a registration in the no-open-callback state. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] no-open-request registration; user authorisation for two writes (submit + reschedule).
tcs.steps:
1. Log in (8888888888 / 147258) and land on Home.
2. Click 'Schedule a Call'.
3. Keep/choose a Preferred Date & Time, add a comment, click Submit Request.
4. Confirm the header now reads 'Call Requested'.
5. Click 'Call Requested', change the Preferred Date & Time, click Reschedule.
tcs.expected: The request is created (status REQUESTED, linked to the registration) and the header flips to 'Call Requested'; the Reschedule modal opens with the existing data; the rescheduled date/time is saved and the header still reads 'Call Requested'. (Verify both writes per note 8.)

tcs.scenario: To verify the request -> SM schedule -> feedback E2E
tcs.description: Verify the cross-surface journey from buyer request through SM scheduling/completion to buyer feedback via the token link.
tcs.precond: A buyer request, an SM able to schedule/complete, and the generated feedback link. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] coordinated SM action; valid feedback link; user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Buyer submits a callback request.
2. SM schedules the meeting (buyer is notified).
3. SM completes the call and submits SM feedback.
4. Buyer opens the /call-feedback/:code link, sets a rating, optionally comments, and submits.
tcs.expected: The request progresses through REQUESTED -> scheduled -> completed; the buyer receives the scheduling notification and the feedback link; submitting feedback sets isBuyerFeedbackSubmitted=true. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the terminal status given the COMPLETED-unreachable drift (BYR_CB_030).
